name: Abijah
overview: Abijah was a male Levite who served as the eighth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of Aaron's sons, distinguishing him from other individuals named Abijah in the Scriptures. This specific priestly role highlights his important function within the Levitical priesthood during the time of the divided priestly courses.
namesAndTitles: The name Abijah means '[my] father is YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew proper name. This name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:10, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant meaning related to the worship of the Lord.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Abijah was a descendant of Ithamar, situating him within a particular Levitical lineage. Additionally, he is connected by inference to Zacharias, suggesting a priestly ancestry that continues into the New Testament period. Beyond these, no further family relationships are explicitly recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Abijah's significance lies in his role as one of the priests chosen to serve in the twenty-four divisions established by King David for temple worship, specifically as the eighth in order from the line of Ithamar. This placement affirms the organized structure God ordained for priestly service and highlights the continuity of the Levitical priesthood. His mention in 1 Chronicles underscores the meticulous care taken in preserving the priestly order, which was essential for maintaining proper worship according to God's commands.
